proposals.evidence: Probable Pashto loan. The compiled Hallberg survey has the exact ūgā garlic form in Charsadda, Swat, Batagram and other locations, alongside ūga in Peshawar and Dir. OPED entry37702 and its pronunciation guide independently attest the Pashto garlic word húẓ̌a; the survey g-form is the relevant comparator, rather than an unexplained direct substitution from ẓ̌. Turner3509 refers to a different older Dameli plant-name kuwŕéi/kuwéŕi, with explicitly uncertain garlic identification, and does not establish ancestry for ūgā. Direction is inferred from the regional match; original Hallberg page104 still needs visual verification.

proposals.evidence: Probable Pashto loan. OPED31931 explicitly attests کورکمن with alternative کورکمان, turmeric. The compiled Hallberg survey includes exact kūrkāmān in its NIG location and closely matching kūrkamān in Dir and other locations. This fits the whole Dameli word much better than directly assigning Sanskrit haridrā or karcūra, whose reflex sets do not explain this form. Borrowing direction remains an inference, and original Hallberg page103 still needs visual verification; no remote plant-name ancestry is asserted.
